title: Sufficiency of Scripture
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The sufficiency of Scripture means that God’s Word gives His people everything needed to know Him, receive salvation, grow in godliness, resist error, and live faithfully before Him. Scripture is sufficient for faith and obedience because God has given what His people need.
summary: The sufficiency of Scripture means that God’s Word gives His people everything needed to know Him, receive salvation, grow in godliness, resist error, and live faithfully before Him. Scripture is sufficient for faith and obedience because God has given what His people need.
christFocus: The Scriptures are sufficient because they reveal Christ, the Gospel, and the way of salvation. Believers do not need another Savior, another Gospel, or another final authority beyond the Word that leads them to Jesus.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
God has not left His people without what they need for faith and godliness. Scripture teaches, reproves, corrects, trains, revives, warns, comforts, and equips. It reveals who God is, what sin is, who Christ is, how sinners are saved, and how believers are called to live.

The sufficiency of Scripture does not mean the Bible answers every possible question about every subject. God has not revealed every hidden thing. But everything necessary for salvation, doctrine, worship, holiness, discipleship, and faithful obedience is given in His Word.

This doctrine also guards against the idea that Scripture must be supplemented by new revelations, human philosophies, secret knowledge, or spiritual trends in order to be useful. God’s Word is not incomplete for the purpose He gave it.

The church must trust Scripture’s sufficiency in ministry. Counseling, preaching, discipleship, correction, restoration, worship, and mission must be shaped by God’s Word rather than by methods that push Scripture to the margins.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
People often look everywhere else before they look to God’s Word. They may chase techniques, trends, personalities, private revelations, or systems that promise deeper life than Scripture gives. This can leave believers spiritually dependent on voices God never appointed as final.

The sufficiency of Scripture gives rest and confidence. God has spoken enough. The broken do not need secret knowledge to find Christ. The tempted do not need novelty to obey God. The church does not need to improve the Gospel to make it powerful.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Return to Scripture as the sufficient Word of God for faith and obedience. Do not despise wise counsel or practical help, but never let anything replace the authority and necessity of God’s Word. Let Scripture shape your view of God, sin, salvation, identity, suffering, restoration, worship, and discipleship.
